brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: handle:0,0,0;top mounted on cover:0,0,0;full;top at center cell (0,0,0) with three inserts; spans the caddy width and is visible from above in look polar 10

Two hex-bin-full-div2 trays: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) - 4 compartments total; staged with heap-screws-div2 props in f9 and f11 compartments visible from top view

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for bits / small fasteners
requirements.evidence: Same divided bins provide second compartments per side for bits; staged with heap-nuts-div3 in f10 and f12 as bit/small-parts stand-ins; 2-compartment bins keep screws and bits separated

finish.summary: Three-cell linear caddy (-1 to +1) with center handle/cover cell and two flanking divided bins (hex-bin-full-div2, 2 compartments each = 4 total). House rules applied: open faces capped (14 solid caps) and joints locked with 2 jointBolts. Props show screws and small fasteners sorted by compartment. Top-down view confirms handle and divided storage are visible and accessible.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
